text:
maria (eng-platform): heads up — customer reported weird billing spike tied to streaming + prefetch sidecar + tool invocation. looks like provisional tokens stuck after a resume/reconnect flow. attaching timeline below.

ajay (eng-runtime): ugh. do we have a minimal repro? which flow — client resume or server reconnect?

maria (eng-platform): client does resume. sequence: 1) client opens stream with x-session-id header 2) sidecar prefetches KV/prefix for fast continuation 3) toolcall invoked mid-stream 4) client times out, reconnects with same session id 5) server resumes but truncated output — last chunk lost 6) client retries, final output returns but ledger shows both provisional and final tokens as charged.

olivia (billing): can you paste the ledger lines? want to see provisional vs confirmed entries.

maria (eng-platform): logs: 
```
ledger: session=abc123 provisional_charge=0.75 tokens reason=streaming_prefetch
ledger: session=abc123 toolcall_charge=0.40 tokens reason=toolcall-exec
ledger: session=abc123 provisional_confirmed=0.00 tokens reason=missing-ack
ledger: session=abc123 final_charge=0.95 tokens reason=final-confirm
```

sam (frontend): client code uses sdk-sidecar that prefetches prefix for kv cache. on reconnect it sends `x-resume-offset`. maybe offset semantics changed after we added truncation-on-toolcall.

ajay (eng-runtime): that rings a bell — we changed toolcall TTL and now the runtime may drop the tail tokens if toolcall didn't ACK quickly. the prefetch path marks prefetched tokens as provisional until final ack. if reconnect happens before final ack, current ledger keeps provisional and then also credits final when response completes. double charge.

jon (observability-bot): telemetry: found ~47 incidents in last week where `provisional_confirmed` flag stayed false for >30s then final_charge doubled. affected customers: 2 enterprise, 1 midmarket. 90% of cases involved sidecar prefetch.

olivia (billing): we should decide policy: either make provisional reversible (auto-reclaim on final) or ensure we never emit provisional until toolcall window is safe. reclaiming requires negative ledger entries which UI currently hides.

maria (eng-platform): UX impact: console shows "charged X tokens" and then later a separate line "provisional Y tokens" — confusing to users. propose we: 1) mark provisional as "pending" in UI but do not count toward displayed spent until settled OR 2) change server so prefetch marks tokens in-memory but not in billing ledger until final ack.

ajay (eng-runtime): option 2 is safer for billing cleanliness but raises risk of under-accounting in fail-stop (if server crashes before final ack we'd lose provisional accounting). we could emit provisional to ledger with `state=pending` and implement auto-reversal once final confirmed. ledger already supports reversal lines but UI needs to surface them.

sam (frontend): quick patch: in console, show a badge "pending tokens" with hover explaining provisional vs confirmed. customers have been pinging support. makes us look better fast.

olivia (billing): we need product + legal signoff on auto-reversal semantics. refunds are OK but we must keep audit trail. if we do reversals we must ensure webhook/usage export includes both entries (provisional and reversal).

ajay (eng-runtime): tech plan I propose: 
- change prefetch to write provisional entries with tags: `prefetch-session`, `prefetch-offset`
- ensure final confirm replaces provisional by writing reversal entry `reversal_of:<id>`; ledger emits both so audit is intact
- adjust router: on reconnect use last-confirmed-offset not last-prefetch-offset (prevents resuming into prefetched-only tokens)
- bump toolcall ack window from 3s -> 6s as a safety margin (config flag per customer)

maria (eng-platform): +1. also add a small event in tracing so we can link session->provisional->reversal in observability UI (currently hard to trace). Jon can we add a quick panel showing provisional churn by model/route?

jon (observability-bot): yes — I can add a heatmap & trace linking. will need sample ids from runtime logs (we already capture `session_id` and `prefetch_id`).

sam (frontend): deploy plan for UI change: show pending tokens in billing panel behind feature-flag. roll to internal first. simple copy: "Pending tokens (may be reversed on resumed/confirmed responses)".

olivia (billing): timeline: we can ship UI flag + ledger reversal support in 2 sprints if eng-runtime approves. need to freeze language with legal. also need a one-off backfill: fix customers hit by double charge last week — should we auto-credit them?

maria (eng-platform): yes, please auto-credit. small number of customers. let's run reconciliation job that finds sessions with both provisional and final where charges overlap and emit credits.

ajay (eng-runtime): will prototype changes this week. plan to add unit tests that simulate: prefetch -> toolcall -> lost chunk -> resume -> final, and assert ledger has provisional+reversal rather than duplicate final.

sam (frontend): i18n note: copy for pending tooltip needs translations. not blocking.

olivia (billing): stepping back: long term I prefer we avoid provisional ledger entries for non-critical short-lived prefetches. consider in-memory only for customers on trial. for enterprise with full SLA we can keep provisional in ledger for transparency.

maria (eng-platform): makes sense. new config flag per customer: `prefetch_billing_mode: [ledger, memory]`. default ledger for now; trial customers memory. add to onboarding checklist.

jon (observability-bot): created ticket: INF-7642 to track runtime + ledger + UI changes. linking logs & a small repro.

maria (eng-platform): thanks all. next steps: ajay to prototype reversal path, sam to mock UI pending badge, olivia to draft legal copy, jon to wire up observability trace. will regroup in 48h. :thumbsup:

quota-bot: automated note: found 2 open sessions older than 24h with `pending` state — queued for reconciliation.
